facts.text: Fort Davis was founded in 1854 on the San Antonio–El Paso Road to guard emigrants, mail coaches, and freight wagons during the Comanche and Mescalero war trails.
Town sits at southeastern foot of Davis Mountains, 4,982 ft high, making it Texas' coolest town.
Fort Davis National Historic Site preserves the original 1854 fort and offers a 15‑minute orientation film at its visitor center.
During holidays and summer, volunteers in period dress reenact history inside the furnished buildings of the historic site.
The site is part of the Greater Big Dawn International Dark Sky Reserve, where stargazers can see the Milky Way in full glory.
Fort Davis is the county seat of Jeff Davis County, the highest‑elevation county seat in Texas at 4,900 ft.
